rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says Nāfiʿ retains the alif in أنا أحيي وأميت but considers this reading baseless.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: على أن نافعا قد أثبت الألف

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki reports the Basran analysis: the pronoun is hamza and nūn, while an extra alif reinforces it.
rows.anchor: قال مكي: والألف زائدة عند البصريين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the alif was added at pause to make the nūn's vowel clear.
rows.anchor: وقيل: زيدت للوقف لتظهر حركة النون

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans treat أنا as the full pronoun and Nāfiʿ's alif as original; others delete it for lightness because the fatḥa indicates it.
rows.anchor: والاسم عند الكوفيين «أنا» بكماله

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawharī calls أنا a first-person singular pronoun, built on fatḥ to distinguish it from أن, a particle governing the verb; the final alif marks the vowel at pause and normally drops medially, except in a poor dialect, as the poem shows.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري: وأما قولهم «أنا» فهو اسم مكنى

rows.speaker: النحاس وغيره
rows.claim: Forms بهت, بهت, and بهت mean that someone was confounded, fell silent, and became perplexed.
rows.anchor: وبهت الرجل وبهت وبهت إذا انقطع وسكت متحيرا

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that some Arabs used بهت with fatḥa on both letters for this meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: وحكي عن بعض العرب في هذا المعنى «بهت»

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads فبهت with fatḥa on bāʾ and ḍamma on hāʾ, a dialect variant of the form with kasra on hāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني قرأ أبو حيوة:

rows.speaker: ابن السميقع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ reads both letters with fatḥa, meaning Abraham confounded the unbeliever and making الذي accusative; it may also be a dialect form.
rows.anchor: قال: وقرأ ابن السميقع «فبهت» بفتح الباء والهاء

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash reports a kasra on hāʾ, like غرق and دهش; most readers use ḍamma there.
rows.anchor: قال: وحكى أبو الحسن الأخفش قراءة «فبهت» بكسر الهاء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says some understood the fatḥa reading as abuse and slander: Nimrod cursed after being silenced and left helpless.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقد تأول قوم في قراءة من قرأ «فبهت» بفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reports God's detailed knowledge of everything; He knows what was, what will be, and what would not be, as many Qur'anic passages say.
rows.anchor: هذا خبر عن علمه تعالى بالأشياء على التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because nothing is hidden from God, Jesus cannot be God or God's son, since things are hidden from him.
rows.anchor: فكيف يكون عيسى إلها أو ابن إله وهو تخفى عليه الأشياء

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says الكتاب means writing and script.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: الكتاب الكتابة والخط.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies الكتاب as a book other than the Torah and Gospel that God taught Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو كتاب غير التوراة والإنجيل علمه الله عيسى عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ورسولا can mean that God makes Jesus a messenger, that he speaks to them as a messenger, or that it is coordinated with وجيها.
rows.anchor: أي ونجعله رسولا. أو يكلمهم رسولا.

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash allows the wāw to be extra and رسول to be a circumstantial accusative referring to Jesus: God teaches him the book as a messenger.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: وإن شئت جعلت الواو في قوله «ورسولا» مقحمة

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: The long report of Abū Dharr says Moses was the first prophet of the Israelites and Jesus the last.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث أبي ذر الطويل. «وأول أنبياء بني إسرائيل موسى وآخرهم عيسى عليه السلام».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here أخلق means to shape or fashion, or to estimate, for the Israelites.
rows.anchor: أي أصور وأقدر لكم

rows.speaker: الأعرج وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj and Abū Jaʿfar read كهيئة as كهية with doubled yāʾ; other readers use the hamza.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعرج وأبو جعفر «كهية» بالتشديد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word الطير may be masculine or feminine.
rows.anchor: والطير يذكر ويؤنث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun فيه may refer to the single bird, the birds, or the clay, which becomes a flying creature; طائر and طير compare to تاجر and تجر.
rows.anchor: أي في الواحد منه أو منها أو في الطين

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says the bird flew while people watched but fell dead when out of sight, distinguishing God's creative act from Jesus's.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says Jesus made only the bat, whose complete and unusual animal-like features made it a striking sign of power; challengers asked him to animate one, and it flew after his breath.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لم يخلق غير الخفاش لأنه أكمل الطير خلقا ليكون أبلغ في القدرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The bat is flesh and blood yet flies without feathers, gives live birth and has a milk-producing udder, teeth, ears, menstruation, and unusual vision; it is said to laugh like a human too.
rows.anchor: ومن عجائبه أنه لحم ودم يطير بغير ريش ويلد كما يلد الحيوان ولا يبيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that account, Jesus shaped the clay and breathed, but God created the creature, as Gabriel's breath also precedes God's creation.
rows.anchor: وكان تسوية الطين والنفخ من عيسى والخلق من الله

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ruʾba's line uses الأكمه for one blind from birth.
rows.anchor: فارتد ارتداد الأكمه وقال ابن فارس:

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris says الكمه is blindness from birth, though it can occur later, and cites Suwayd's poem as evidence.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فارس: الكمه العمى يولد به الإنسان وقد يعرض

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the akmah sees during the day but not at night.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: هو الذي يبصر بالنهار ولا يبصر بالليل.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima calls him weak-sighted, but says linguistically the word means blindness, as in the cited verb forms.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: هو الأعمش، ولكنه في اللغة العمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baras is the familiar white skin affliction; al-abrass al-qamar and sāmm abras are named creatures, and its plural is الأبارص.
rows.anchor: والبرص معروف وهو بياض يعتري الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These two diseases are singled out because they were incurable; since medicine predominated in Jesus's era, God gave him a miracle in that field.
rows.anchor: وخص هذان بالذكر لأنهما عياءان.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An account the author leaves uncertain says Jesus revived four people: al-ʿĀdhir, a widow's son, a tax collector's daughter, and Noah's son Sam.
rows.anchor: قيل: أحيا أربعة أنفس: العاذر وكان صديقا له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Al-ʿĀdhir, Jesus's friend, had died days earlier; Jesus prayed and he rose with his jugular dripping, lived, and had a child.
rows.anchor: فأما العاذر فإنه كان قد توفي قبل ذلك بأيام فدعا الله فقام بإذن الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A widow's son being carried on a bier rose at Jesus's prayer, dressed, carried the bier on his neck, and returned home.
rows.anchor: وأما ابن العجوز فإنه مر به يحمل على سريره فدعا الله فقام ولبس ثيابه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A tax collector's daughter, dead since the previous night, revived at Jesus's prayer and later had a child.
rows.anchor: وأما بنت العاشر فكان أتى عليها ليلة فدعا الله فعاشت بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: When people challenged Jesus to revive Noah's son Sam, Sam emerged gray-haired; he said the call made him fear the Resurrection and death's agony still gripped his throat after more than four thousand years.
rows.anchor: فخرج من قبره وقد شاب رأسه. فقال له عيسى: كيف شاب رأسك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Sam's revival persuaded some to believe, while others rejected it as magic.
rows.anchor: فقال للقوم: صدقوه فإنه نبي فآمن به بعضهم وكذبه بعضهم

rows.speaker: إسمعيل ابن عياش
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh says Jesus prayed two cycles, reciting Sūrat al-Mulk then al-Sajda, and invoked seven names.
rows.anchor: وروي من حديث إسمعيل ابن عياش قال: حدثني محمد بن طلحة عن رجل

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī includes the prayer report but says its chain is not strong.
rows.anchor: ذكره البيهقي وقال: ليس إسناده بالقوي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنبئكم means telling them what they ate and stored. After the resurrections they asked for another sign: what they ate at home and saved for tomorrow.
rows.anchor: أي بالذي تأكلونه وما تدخرون. وذلك أنهم لما أحيا لهم الموتى

rows.speaker: مجاهد والزهري والسختياني
rows.claim: Mujāhid, al-Zuhrī, and al-Sakhtiyānī read وما تذخرون with dhāl and without doubling.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد والزهري والسختياني «وما تذخرون» بالذال المعجمة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وغيره
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and others say Jesus told schoolchildren what they had stored, so their fathers stopped them sitting with him.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وغيره: كان يخبر الصبيان في الكتاب بما يدخرون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Jesus told them what they had eaten from the table and secretly stored from it.
rows.anchor: قتادة: أخبرهم بما أكلوه من المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars unanimously regard the verse as definitive, agreed upon, and unabrogated; the author says it is likewise in all scriptures and reason alone would recognize its authority.
rows.anchor: أجمع العلماء على أن هذه الآية من المحكم المتفق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is submission and need before the one with judgment and choice; God commands exclusive devotion, making the verse a foundation for cleansing deeds of ostentation and other impurities.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى معنى العبودية وهي التذلل والافتقار، لمن له الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links sincerity to the warning that one hoping to meet the Lord must do good and associate no one in worship.
rows.anchor: فمن كان يرجو لقآء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the declaration that pure religion belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: ألا لله الدين الخالص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship God is linked to the command to worship Him sincerely in religion.
rows.anchor: ومآ أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين

rows.speaker: بعض علمائنا
rows.claim: Some scholars say purification for cooling or fasting to settle one's stomach does not fulfill worship if a worldly aim is mixed into devotion; God accepts only pure work.
rows.anchor: قال بعض علمائنا: إنه من تطهر تبردا أو صام محما لمعدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An imam who senses someone entering during bowing should not wait, since waiting would make the bowing no longer solely for God.
rows.anchor: وكذلك إذا أحس الرجل بداخل في الركوع وهو إمام لم ينتظره

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In a Muslim hadith qudsī, God says that whoever performs a deed while associating another with Him is left to that partner and the deed.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Al-Dāraquṭnī reports sealed records presented on Judgment Day: God accepts only deeds intended for His sake, even though the angels had seen good in rejected deeds.
rows.anchor: وروى الدارقطني عن أنس بن مالك قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس الفهري
rows.claim: A report from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays al-Fihrī quotes the Prophet: God accepts only what is sincerely for Him, not what is split between Him, kin, or people's approval.
rows.anchor: وروي أيضا عن الضحاك بن قيس الفهري قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: The scholars classify shirk as three forbidden degrees. The greatest is believing in a partner in divinity, the pre-Islamic form, warned against at 4:48.
rows.anchor: مسألة إذا ثبت هذا فاعلم أن علماءنا رضي الله عنهم قالوا: الشرك على ثلاث مراتب

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: The second degree is belief that another independently brings an act into existence, even without calling it a god; the scholars call the Qadariyya the community's Magians, and Ibn ʿUmar disavowed them in the Gabriel report.
rows.anchor: ويليه في الرتبة اعتقاد شريك لله تعالى في الفعل، وهو قول

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: The third degree is ostentation: doing worship commanded for God for someone else. It invalidates deeds and is subtle; these verses and reports are cited to prohibit it.
rows.anchor: ويلي هذه الرتبة الإشراك في العبادة وهو الرياء

rows.speaker: المحاسبي
rows.claim: Al-Muḥāsibī explains in al-Riʿāya how ostentation corrupts deeds.
rows.anchor: فقد أوضحه في كتابه «الرعاية»

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد بن أبي فضالة الأنصاري
rows.claim: Ibn Mājah reports the Companion Abū Saʿīd ibn Abī Faḍāla: on Judgment Day, those who shared a deed intended for God with another should seek the other's reward, since God needs no partners.
rows.anchor: وفي سنن ابن ماجه عن أبي سعيد بن أبي فضالة الأنصاري

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet calls hidden shirk more fearful than the Antichrist: someone beautifies his prayer because another person is watching.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: A report from Shaddād ibn Aws says the Prophet feared shirk for his community, meaning deeds for others and hidden desire, not worship of celestial bodies or idols; al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm transmitted it.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن شداد بن أوس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Asked about hidden desire, the Prophet defines it as learning knowledge because one wants people to gather around him.
rows.anchor: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الشهوة الخفية فقال:

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Sahl al-Tustarī's first kind of ostentation begins with acting for someone other than God while seeking to appear devout; he calls this hypocrisy and doubt in faith.
rows.anchor: قال سهل بن عبد الله التستري رضي الله عنه: الرياء على ثلاثة وجوه

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Sahl's second kind begins sincerely for God, then gains energy when seen; if the person repents, he says all those deeds must be repeated.
rows.anchor: والآخر يدخل في الشيء لله فإذا اطلع عليه غير الله نشط، فهذا إذا تاب

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Sahl's third kind starts sincerely for God and ends in recognition and pleasure at praise; this is the ostentation God forbids.
rows.anchor: والثالث دخل في العمل بالإخلاص وخرج به لله فعرف بذلك ومدح عليه

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqmān tells his son that ostentation seeks the reward of deeds in this world, while the people worked for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال لقمان لابنه: الرياء أن تطلب ثواب عملك في دار الدنيا

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Sahl's remedy is to conceal deeds: perform what must be public sincerely, and prefer no one but God see what need not be shown.
rows.anchor: قيل له: فما دواء الرياء؟ قال كتمان العمل

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Sahl says not to count a deed seen by other people as a true deed of devotion.
rows.anchor: قال: وكل عمل اطلع عليه الخلق فلا تعده من العمل.

rows.speaker: أيوب السختياني
rows.claim: Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī says no sensible person wants others to know where his deeds stand.
rows.anchor: وقال أيوب السختياني: ما هو بعاقل من أحب أن يعرف مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahl's third kind is blameworthy when pleasure in praise seeks rank, affection, or material gain, because the heart delights in exposure even if it came after the deed.
rows.anchor: إن كان سكونه وسروره إليهم لتحصل منزلته في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God reveals a deed against the person's wishes, joy in God's favor is obedience, as the verse commands joy in His bounty and mercy.
rows.anchor: فأما من أطلع الله عليه خلقه وهو لا يحب اطلاعهم عليه فيسر بصنع الله

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Asked about a hadith of concealing a deed that pleases one when revealed, Sahl says the pleasure is gratitude that God made it known.
rows.anchor: وقد سئل سهل عن حديث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God pairs gratitude to parents with gratitude to Him; the author cites the command to thank God and one's parents.
rows.anchor: أن اشكر لي ولوالديك

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says the Prophet taught that God's pleasure is in parents' pleasure and His anger in their anger.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the discussion of relatives, orphans, and the poor has already appeared in Sūrat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى الكلام فيه في «البقرة».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands preserving the neighbor, fulfilling the neighbor's rights, and respecting the neighbor's protected status, emphasizing the neighbor after parents and kin.
rows.anchor: أما الجار فقد أمر الله تعالى بحفظه والقيام بحقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ذي القربى is the close neighbor and الجنب the stranger; the author notes this is Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: أي الغريب قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Lexicographers cite a poem using جنابة for distance and being a stranger, evidence for الجنب as a distant neighbor.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أهل اللغة: فلا تحرمني نائلا عن جنابة

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse also uses عن جنابة for distance or being a stranger.
rows.anchor: وقال الأعشى: أتيت حريثا زائرا عن جنابة

rows.speaker: الأعمش والمفضل
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and al-Mufaḍḍal read الجار الجنب with fatḥa on jīm and a still nūn; related dialects mean having no kinship, with أجانب as plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش والمفضل «والجار الجنب» بفتح الجيم وسكون النون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another analysis assumes an omitted noun: والجار ذي الجنب, the neighbor of the side or area.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على تقدير حذف المضاف، أي والجار ذي الجنب أي ذي الناحية.

rows.speaker: نوف الشامي
rows.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī identifies the close neighbor as Muslim and the distant neighbor as Jewish or Christian; the author says neighborly care is recommended for Muslims and non-Muslims alike, the correct view.
rows.anchor: وقال نوف الشامي: { والجار ذي القربى } المسلم { والجار الجنب } اليهودي والنصراني.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neighborly kindness may mean material support or good companionship, refraining from harm, and defending the neighbor.
rows.anchor: والإحسان قد يكون بمعنى المواساة، وقد يكون بمعنى حسن العشرة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In a Bukhārī report from ʿĀʾisha, the Prophet says Gabriel kept enjoining care for the neighbor until he thought the neighbor would inherit.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري عن عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: أبو شريح
rows.claim: The Prophet swears three times that one whose neighbor is not safe from his harms lacks complete faith; this applies to every neighbor and requires avoiding harm.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي شريح أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A prophetic report assigns three rights to a Muslim relative neighbor, two to a Muslim neighbor without kinship, and one to a non-Muslim neighbor: the right of neighborliness.
rows.anchor: الجيران ثلاثة فجار له ثلاثة حقوق وجار له حقان

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: When ʿĀʾisha asked which of two neighbors should receive her gift, the Prophet told her to choose the one with the nearer door.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: قلت يا رسول الله، إن لي جارين فإلى أيهما أهدي

rows.speaker: جماعة من العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars take close and distant neighbors to mean those with near and far homes, using the gift report to support a neighbor's preemption right and the hadith about a neighbor's claim to adjoining property.
rows.anchor: فذهب جماعة من العلماء إلى أن هذا الحديث يفسر المراد من قوله تعالى: { والجار ذي القربى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that inference: ʿĀʾisha asked whom to gift first, and the Prophet prioritized the nearer door; the report also shows neighbor can mean more than an adjoining house.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة في ذلك، فإن عائشة رضي الله عنها إنما سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa denies preemption to a neighbor without shared wall or route if the adjoining neighbor relinquishes it.
rows.anchor: وقد خرج أبو حنيفة عن ظاهر هذا الحديث فقال: إن الجار اللصيق إذا ترك الشفعة

rows.speaker: عوام العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars say a bequest to neighbors includes adjoining and non-adjoining neighbors; Abū Ḥanīfa limits it to the adjoining neighbor.
rows.anchor: وعوام العلماء يقولون: إذا أوصى الرجل لجيرانه أعطى اللصيق وغيره

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي وابن شهاب
rows.claim: Al-Awzāʿī and Ibn Shihāb define the neighborhood as forty houses in every direction.
rows.anchor: فكان الأوزاعي يقول: أربعون دارا من كل ناحية وقاله ابن شهاب.

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet sent Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAlī to announce that forty houses count as neighbors and that none enters Paradise if a neighbor is unsafe from his harm.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني نزلت محلة قوم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib says anyone who hears the call to prayer is a neighbor.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: من سمع النداء فهو جار.

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group defines a mosque's neighbor as anyone who hears the call to begin prayer.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: من سمع إقامة الصلاة فهو جار ذلك المسجد.

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says anyone sharing a quarter or city with a person is a neighbor.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: من ساكن رجلا في محلة أو مدينة فهو جار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links neighborhood to the verse saying the hypocrites would not remain in Medina except briefly, so their common residence counts as neighborliness.
rows.anchor: ثم لا يجاورونك فيها إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neighbor relations have degrees, some closer than others; the nearest is one's wife, as the cited line calls her a neighbor.
rows.anchor: والجيرة مراتب بعضها ألصق من بعض، أدناها الزوجة

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Muslim reports Abū Dharr's account of the Prophet advising him to add water to broth and look after his neighbors.
rows.anchor: ما رواه مسلم عن أبي ذر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharing food builds affection, good relations, and mutual help; cooking smells can distress neighbors and their hungry children, especially where the caregiver is poor or widowed.
rows.anchor: فحض عليه السلام على مكارم الأخلاق لما يترتب عليها من المحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharing food prevents distress caused by cooking smells and children's hunger; the author mentions Jacob's separation from Joseph as similar sorrow.
rows.anchor: وكل هذا يندفع بتشريكهم في شيء من الطبيخ يدفع إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The near neighbor is especially suited to a gift because each sees what enters and leaves the other's house and can respond quickly to unexpected needs.
rows.anchor: ولهذا المعنى حض عليه السلام الجار القريب بالهدية لأنه ينظر إلى ما يدخل دار جاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding water is a tactful way to make generosity easy for a miser: water costs nothing, unlike extra meat.
rows.anchor: نبه بذلك على تيسير الأمر على البخيل تنبيها لطيفا

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: The cited couplet says the poet's cooking pot and his neighbor's are one, and it is raised to the neighbor before his own.
rows.anchor: ولقد أحسن القائل: قدري وقدر الجار واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gift should be a customary amount, not a contemptibly small portion; if only a little is available, give it without disdain, and the recipient should accept it.
rows.anchor: ولا يهدي النزر اليسير المحتقر لقوله عليه السلام:

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet tells believing women not to disdain giving a neighbor a gift, even a roasted sheep's hoof; Mālik transmits it in his Muwaṭṭaʾ.
rows.anchor: أخرجه مالك في موطئه. وكذا قيدناه «يا نساء المؤمنات»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the nominative يا نساء المؤمنات without annexation: the vocative يا أيها is omitted, النساء modifies أيها, and المؤمنات modifies النساء; the annexed reading is also reported but less common.
rows.anchor: وكذا قيدناه «يا نساء المؤمنات» بالرفع على غير الإضافة، والتقدير: يا أيها النساء المؤمنات

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet forbids preventing a neighbor from setting a beam in one's wall; Abū Hurayra threatens to cast the ruling among listeners. Variants include singular or plural خشبه and أكنافكم or أكتافكم.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase لأرمين بها means that Abū Hurayra would throw the saying or case among them.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «لأرمين بها» أي بالكلمة والقصة.

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهما
rows.claim: Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa, and their companions read the beam report as recommending kindness, not imposing a duty, since property is forbidden without willing consent; they compare it to the recommendation not to bar a wife from the mosque.
rows.anchor: فذهب مالك وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهما إلى أن معناه الندب إلى بر الجار

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق وأبو ثور وداود بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, Abū Thawr, Dāwūd, and hadith scholars hold allowing the beam obligatory; Abū Hurayra's insistence supports that he understood a duty.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأصحابه وأحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق وأبو ثور وداود بن علي

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar ruled that Muḥammad ibn Maslama must let al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Khalīfa's channel cross his land, even threatening to force him; Mālik transmits the ruling.
rows.anchor: وهو مذهب عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه فإنه قضى على محمد بن مسلمة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues in al-Radd that Mālik recorded no Companion opposing ʿUmar and criticizes him for recording the ruling without adopting it.
rows.anchor: وزعم الشافعي في كتاب «الرد» أن مالكا لم يرو عن أحد من الصحابة خلاف عمر

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abū ʿUmar rejects al-Shāfiʿī: Muḥammad ibn Maslama, the Anṣār, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf opposed ʿUmar in related watercourse disputes. With Companions divided, reason returns to the rule that Muslim property is inviolable without consent.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: ليس كما زعم الشافعي لأن محمد بن مسلمة كان رأيه في ذلك خلاف رأي عمر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra's statement that he would cast the ruling among them indicates disagreement over whether the permission is obligatory.
rows.anchor: ويدل على الخلاف في ذلك قول أبي هريرة: مالي أراكم عنها معرضين
